extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: Vibravox is a GDPR-compliant dataset of French speech captured with five different body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) along with a reference airborne microphone. It contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer. The dataset comprises four subsets: speech-clean, speech-noisy, speechless-clean, and speechless-noisy, with annotations on recording conditions and linguistic/phonetic transcriptions.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, Éric Bavu
extraction.publisher: Laboratoire de Mécanique des Structures et des Systèmes Couplés, Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (Cnam); French-German Research Institute of Saint-Louis (ISL)
extraction.citeAs: Hauret, J., Olivier, M., Joubaud, T., Langrenne, C., Poirée, S., Zimpfer, V., & Bavu, É. (2024). Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors. arXiv:2407.11828.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected through a rigorous recording protocol involving 200 participants (188 retained after post-processing). Participants wore six audio sensors simultaneously (five body-conduction sensors and one airborne reference microphone) and performed four sequential recording steps: reading French Wikipedia sentences for 15 minutes (speech-clean), remaining silent in noisy environment for 2m24s (speechless-noisy), remaining silent in quiet environment for 54s (speechless-clean), and speaking in noisy environment for 54s (speech-noisy). Recordings used a Zoom F8n field recorder at 48 kHz, 32-bit resolution. Noise was spatialized using a 56-loudspeaker spherical array (1.07m radius) with 3D ambisonics.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Direct measurement, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A small number of audio clips had deficiencies including mispronounced sentences, sensors shifting from initial positions, sensor malfunctions, or unequipped microphones. Out of 200 participants, 12 were excluded (6%), and 6.8% of pronounced sentences were filtered out. Three automatic filters were applied: PER filter (>10% discarded), SNR filter (<1.5 dB discarded), and sensitivity drift filter.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text for reading originated from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice. Ambient noise samples were sourced from Audio Set (focused on battlefield and industrial environments) and in-house recordings of concerts and street events in 3rd and 5th order ambisonics. Audio was recorded directly from six sensors worn by participants.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Text normalization operations including lowercasing and removing punctuation (except apostrophes). Phonetic transcription generated using International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) with 33 French phonemes via the CoML lab text phonemizer. Manual phonetic transcription for unrecognized words. A 20 Hz high-pass filter was uniformly applied to each acquisition channel to attenuate low-frequency noise.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Three automatic filters were applied: (1) PER filter discarding samples with PER > 10% based on comparison between labeled transcription and Whisper-timestamped output; (2) SNR filter checking Lspeech50 - Lsilence50 > 1.5 dB; (3) Sensitivity drift filter checking Lspeech50[i,j] > Lsilence50[i]. Voice Activity Detection timestamps were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides, with 15 ms trimming if boundaries were exceeded. Dataset split by speaker: 80% train, 10% validation, 10% test, balanced by gender.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Textual data from French Wikipedia was filtered to exclude proper names (retaining only common first names, French town/region names, country names), numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, and syntactic errors. Phonetic transcription using IPA with 33 French phonemes was generated via automated phonemizer with manual correction for unrecognized words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: CoML lab text phonemizer (Phonemizer library); whisper-timestamped model for Voice Activity Detection and alignment
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Levenshtein distance used to compute Phoneme Error Rate between labeled transcription and Whisper output for filtering quality. Manual phonetic transcription was applied for words producing language switches in the automated phonemizer.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: whisper-timestamped (speech-to-text with dynamic time warping), Phonemizer library from CoML lab, Voice Activity Detection
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset is publicly released on HuggingFace (https://huggingface.co/datasets/Cnam-LMSSC/vibravox) under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license. Version revision 071945b referenced.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Participants' voice recordings, gender (97 Female / 91 Male), and age information (mean 28.55 years, range 18-82). All data collection complied with GDPR, with informed consent obtained, data anonymized and encrypted.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance research in body-conducted speech capture for robust communication in noisy environments, with applications in military operations, industrial settings, voice commands, and vital sign monitoring. Potential applications include access control, intelligence gathering, and battlefield forensics. Speaker verification capabilities raise biometric privacy considerations.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited to French language speech. Participant age distribution is skewed toward younger participants (median 25 years). The in-ear microphone sensors may have acoustic sealing issues for certain ear canal anatomies (one-size-fits-all design). The Lombard effect may cause speakers to increase vocal effort in noisy conditions, which affects signal-to-external-noise ratio estimates.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limited to French language. The speech-noisy subset is relatively small (1h34m training) and lacks a clean reference, making it suitable primarily for testing rather than training speech enhancement models. The 'one-size-fits-all' in-ear microphone design does not fit all ear canal anatomies properly. The temple vibration sensor has very narrow bandwidth. Post-processing filtering excluded 6% of participants and 6.8% of sentences to ensure quality. Dataset size (45h per sensor) is not the largest compared to ESMB (128h).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing for three key speech processing tasks: (1) Speech Enhancement / Bandwidth Extension, (2) Speech-to-Phonemes Recognition / ASR, (3) Speaker Verification. Additional potential applications include heart rate tracking, vital signs monitoring, voice commands, and synthetic dataset generation with realistic physiological noise. The speech-clean subset is the primary training set; speech-noisy serves mainly for testing; speechless-clean provides sensor noise characterization; speechless-noisy enables data augmentation by mixing with clean speech.
